# Native codec fixtures

`half-red-blue.heic` and `half-red-blue.avif` are generated 64 × 64 images: the top 32 rows are red and the bottom 32 rows are blue. No third-party artwork or metadata is included. They were encoded with macOS 26.6.2 ImageIO through `sips -s format heic` / `sips -s format avif` from a deterministic RGB PNG on September 9, 2026.

The decoder tests use misleading filenames deliberately. They verify container-byte routing, native codec decoding, dimensions, bounded resizing, and top/bottom orientation, allowing lossy color variation. Full rendering requires compatible macOS ImageIO codecs; Linux has a precise unsupported-codec fallback.

`half-red-blue.jp2` uses the same deterministic 64 × 64 RGB pattern, encoded with
macOS ImageIO `sips -s format jp2`. `half-red-blue.j2k` is its extracted `jp2c`
codestream. Both contain only generated test pixels and test supplied-byte
JPEG 2000 detection, rendering, orientation, and bounded resize independently
from their filename. No original artwork or private metadata is included.

Historical macOS 26.6.2 validation rendered both JPEG 2000 fixtures. A separate
[macOS 15.7.9 native probe](../../../../docs/benchmarks/jpeg2000-macos15-20260914.json)
([hosted run](https://github.com/FernandoX7/GitTurtle/actions/runs/34886145319))
rendered JP2 with correct dimensions and red/blue orientation through both direct
ImageIO and thumbnail APIs; both APIs returned no image for raw J2K. Recognition
as `public.jpeg-2000` alone does not establish raw-codestream rendering support.

The JP2 test always requires native pixels on macOS. The raw J2K test independently
probes direct ImageIO decoding of this fixed 64 × 64 fixture: a capable codec must
pass every production pixel, dimension, orientation and resize assertion; an
incapable codec must produce the exact unsupported result while byte detection
still overrides the misleading filename. Source-creation or unexpected-dimension
failures in that probe fail the test. There is no OS-version or environment skip.

# Linux helper AVIF and JPEG 2000 fixtures

The `avif-*` and `jpeg2000-*` files are generated by
[`scripts/create-image-codec-fixtures.py`](../../../../scripts/create-image-codec-fixtures.py)
from deterministic pixels written by the script itself; nothing is downloaded or
copied from a third party. Regenerate with `python3 scripts/create-image-codec-fixtures.py`
(`--check` compares without writing). Generated on 2026-11-03 on the AArch64 Arch
development host with libaom's `aomenc` 3.15.0 (`--allintra --limit=1 --threads=1
--cpu-used=6 --end-usage=q --cq-level=8`), OpenJPEG 2.5.4's `opj_compress`
(lossless 5/3 unless noted) and Pillow 13.0.0 with libavif 1.4.2. The script's own
AVIF writer (AVIF 1.1 / MIAF: `ftyp`, `meta` with `hdlr`, `pitm`, `iloc`, `iinf`,
`iref` and `iprp`, then `mdat`) and JP2 writer wrap the encoder output wherever no
encoder writes the shape. Every byte is reproducible except the animation, whose
`moov` carries Pillow's creation time.

Unless noted, images are 64 × 48 in four quadrants: top-left red (220, 30, 30),
top-right green (30, 200, 60), bottom-left blue (30, 50, 220) and bottom-right
near-white (240, 240, 240). "Alpha" means an opaque left half and alpha 128 on the
right half. AVIF colour is BT.601 limited-range YCbCr; tests allow 12 levels of
lossy error (40 with film grain), JPEG 2000 2 (lossless), 16 (subsampled chroma)
or 10 (lossy).

| File | Made by | Expected through `serve` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `avif-yuv420-8bit-alpha.avif` | aomenc 8-bit 4:2:0; alpha as a 4:0:0 auxiliary item; `nclx` 1/13/6 limited | 64 × 48 quadrants with straight alpha |
| `avif-yuv444-10bit-premultiplied.avif` | aomenc 10-bit 4:4:4 (profile 1) of colour premultiplied by the alpha; 10-bit alpha; `prem` reference | the same quadrants, alpha unpremultiplied to straight |
| `avif-yuv420-12bit-alpha.avif` | aomenc 12-bit 4:2:0 (profile 2; aomenc 3.15 cannot set 4:4:4 at 12 bits); 12-bit alpha | the same quadrants with alpha |
| `avif-yuv400-8bit.avif`, `-10bit`, `-12bit` | aomenc `--monochrome` of a limited-range grey ramp; no `colr`, so matrix and range come from the sequence header | grey 0 at x 0, about 130 at x 32, 255 at x 63 |
| `avif-irot-imir.avif` | 8-bit 4:2:0 with essential `irot` 1 (90° anticlockwise) and `imir` 1 (left and right exchanged) | 48 × 64 (original 48 × 64): top-left white, top-right green, bottom-left blue, bottom-right red |
| `avif-film-grain.avif` | aomenc `--film-grain-test=1` | the quadrants with grain applied |
| `avif-display-p3.avif` | quadrants (200, 80, 60), (60, 180, 90), (70, 90, 200), (128, 128, 128) in Display P3, `nclx` 12/13/6 | converted to sRGB: (216, 69, 50), (0, 183, 78), (64, 91, 207), (128, 128, 128) |
| `avif-display-p3-icc.avif` | the same pixels with a `colr` of type `prof` holding the JP2 fixture's minimal ICC v2 Display P3 profile (2.2 gamma), beside `nclx` 1/13/6 | converted by the profile with moxcms: (218, 67, 47), (0, 185, 77), (62, 90, 209), (129, 129, 129), with no flag; the test patches the profile's signature, tag count or colour space, and each draws the stored values with "colour profile not applied" |
| `avif-animation.avif` | Pillow `save_all` of two frames (the quadrants, then reversed), libavif with its primary still item and an `avis` track | the first frame, flagged as an animation |
| `avif-sequence-without-still.avif` | the animation with `ftyp` `avis` (its `avif` and `mif1` brands, which require a primary item, removed) and a `meta` of only its `hdlr`, padded with `free` so the track's offsets hold; `moov` times zeroed | `mp4parse` reads the track and no primary item: `AvifNoStill` |
| `avif-grid.avif` | a `grid` primary item (2 × 2, 64 × 48 output) over four hidden 32 × 24 aomenc tiles, one quadrant colour each, by `dimg` | `mp4parse` reports the grid and exposes no tiles: `AvifGrid` |
| `avif-frame-larger-than-ispe.avif` | hostile: 64 × 64 `ispe` over a grey frame whose sequence header the script rewrites to 16384 × 16384 (security review question 5) | refused by dav1d's `frame_size_limit` with `AvifSizeMismatch`, before the frame is allocated |
| `avif-alpha-smaller-than-image.avif` | hostile: a 32 × 32 alpha item (with its own 32 × 32 `ispe`) under the 64 × 48 image | `AvifSizeMismatch`; with its `ispe` patched to 64 × 48 in the test, the decoded picture is refused the same way |
| `avif-reserved-colour.avif` | hostile: the 8-bit 4:2:0 quadrants with no `colr`, their sequence header's colour description rewritten to the reserved primaries 0, transfer 0 and matrix 3 | passes every check before decoding and libdav1d decodes it; dav1d-rs 0.11.1 reaches `unreachable!()` reading the signalled colour, and `serve` returns that panic as `DecoderFailed` (the AVIF counterpart of the real `hayro-jpeg2000` panic) |
| `jpeg2000-rgb.jp2`, `jpeg2000-rgb.j2k` | `opj_compress` of a PPM | the quadrants exactly |
| `jpeg2000-grey16.jp2` | `opj_compress` of a 16-bit PGM ramp (0 to 65535 across the width) | 8-bit grey 0, 130, 255 at x 0, 32, 63 |
| `jpeg2000-alpha.jp2` | `opj_compress` of an RGBA PAM (no `cdef`: a fourth component beside an sRGB `colr` is read as alpha) | the quadrants with alpha; the tests add a `cdef` |
| `jpeg2000-display-p3-icc.jp2` | the Display P3 quadrants as a J2K, wrapped with a `colr` method 2 holding the script's minimal ICC v2 profile (Display P3 primaries adapted to D50, 2.2 gamma) | converted to sRGB: (218, 67, 47), (0, 185, 77), (62, 90, 209), (129, 129, 129) |
| `jpeg2000-palette.jp2` | `opj_compress` of an 8-bit index PGM (0 to 3 by quadrant), wrapped with `pclr` (4 entries, 3 columns of 8 bits) and `cmap` | the quadrants exactly, at full resolution |
| `jpeg2000-subsampled.jp2` | sYCC (`colr` 18): full-resolution Y and 2 × 2 subsampled Cb and Cr from a raw input (`-F 64,48,3,8,u@1x1:2x2:2x2`) | decoded at full resolution, then 32 × 24 at edge 32 |
| `jpeg2000-large.jp2` | 1024 × 768 gradient (red by x, green by y, blue 128), `-r 100 -n 6` | at edge 128, three resolution levels skipped: 128 × 96 |

The hostile JPEG 2000 inputs (#1549's 97-byte codestream, #1558's 1 × 1 tiles,
#1649's palette, five components, 17-bit samples, JPX without JP2 compatibility)
and the remaining hostile AVIF inputs (`ispe` of 40000 × 1, a missing `ispe`, a
truncated OBU) are patched from these fixtures in the tests that use them, each
citing its source. The grid and the sequence without a still are generated
whole, since `mp4parse` refuses as unreadable a retyped item or a dropped `pitm`
while the `avif` or `mif1` brand promises a primary item.

# Other fixtures

`disposal-transparency.gif` is a generated 4 × 2 indexed-color animation encoded
with Pillow 12.1.1. Its three frames contain red, then green over transparent
pixels, then blue over transparent pixels; delays are 70/90/110 ms and disposal
modes are Keep/Background/Keep. It verifies that transparent overlays retain the
previous canvas and background disposal clears it before the next frame.
